description:
FILED s466bc (Opus) from the #1037 guard-writing.  PRE-EXISTING (verified: the
shape does not reach the drop site on 57848f3 either -- the refusal classifier
is only consulted where a statement was ALREADY dropped).

REPRO:

    use feature 'defer';
    no warnings;
    print "before\n";
    defer { print "deferred\n" }

emits

    (p-void-ctx (pl-defer (p-list-ctx (p-print "deferred\n"))))

-- a call to an undeclared sub `defer` whose ARGUMENT is the block's VALUE.
Nothing is announced.  Add ONE more statement after it and the same file
refuses correctly:

    PCL: refused statement at F line 4: defer { print "deferred\n" } print
    "after\n"; -- defer blocks are not supported

WHY THE DIFFERENCE: PPI joins a block-form `defer` to the statement AFTER it
(the same shape as the format entry, and the reason the drop's source TEXT
spans two statements there).  With a following statement the joined thing is
unlowerable and reaches the drop site, where the ruled classifier sees the
leading `defer` + Block and refuses.  With nothing after it, PPI hands over a
Word + Block that the funcall path lowers happily.

WHY IT MATTERS: docs/not-supported.md \xc2\xa7`defer` says the refusal exists
precisely so the cleanup is not "silently skipped".  In this spelling it IS
silently skipped, AND the block's body runs EAGERLY (perl runs it at scope
exit), so the program is wrong in two directions at once.

FIX SHAPE: the refusal must not depend on whether a statement follows.  A
`defer` + Structure::Block at the head of a statement is the keyword in any
file that has the feature -- the same evidence test `field`/`method`/`ADJUST`
already use (`_class_feature_in_scope`'s sibling).  Route it to
`Pl::Parser::refused_statement_form` (the #1037 builder) rather than adding a
second refusal spelling.

GUARD: Pl/t/refusal-site-01.t row 7b currently uses the TWO-statement spelling
and its comment records why; the fix's guard is the ONE-statement spelling
next to it.
subject: `defer { ... }` that ENDS a file (no statement after it) is not refused and not dropped -- it lowers as a CALL to a sub named `defer`, silently
